post_text:
Four Seasons Resort Megève reopens on 16 December for its first winter as a Palace, the first hotel in Megève to hold the distinction.

Atout France granted the title in June. The resort at Mont d'Arbois has 55 rooms and suites with direct access to the slopes, and three restaurants: La Brasserie Benjamin, Kaito and Idéal 1850 on the mountaintop.

General Manager @Joachim Jacob, who joined the resort in 2019 and rose from director of operations, leads the team. In the kitchens, @Armando Acquaviva signs the Brasserie Benjamin menu and executive pastry chef @Jonathan Chapuy the desserts. At Kaito, chef @Stylianos Chysollari works with sommelier @Ruggero Testori and restaurant manager @Lorenza Vigna.

The novelty this winter is in the 900-square-metre spa. It now offers myBlend treatments by Clarins and says it is the first in France to use the CellSynergy2 device. Chapuy even created the sweet finale of one treatment.

The signal: the Palace label is no longer only a Paris or Riviera story. @Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts now holds it in a ski village, with an estate created for @Edmond de Rothschild, and is using its spa to give returning skiers a reason to book again.

Which ski resort should get the next Palace?

Read the full article: https://hospitality-signals.com/signal-of-the-week/2026-11-04-four-seasons-megeve-palace-winter/
